title: Durable organ xenotransplantation at clinical scale

concept.text: The innovation would make animal organs a dependable, widely available source of long-term replacement organs for people. Its leading example in the supplied evidence is a genetically edited pig kidney that could keep a recipient off dialysis for years, with clinically acceptable risks of rejection, clotting injury, infection and death. The goal combines durable function in living recipients with reliable production and delivery at a scale that materially addresses patient demand.

This is a coordinated transplantation capability: engineering the animal donor, managing the recipient’s immune response, monitoring animal pathogens and producing suitable organs consistently. A xenograft can also provide temporary support until a human organ becomes available. That bridging use is clinically meaningful, but the innovation’s full scope requires dependable long-term replacement, often called destination therapy, together with adequate supply.

significance.text: Human donor-organ scarcity limits transplantation. If animal organs could provide many years of replacement function and be reliably produced and delivered in sufficient numbers, transplantation could become substantially less dependent on the availability of human donors. For kidney recipients, the direct benefit would be sustained freedom from dialysis with acceptable treatment burdens and risks. The reported months of dialysis-free kidney function provide a clinical basis for this possibility, without establishing the long-term outcome.

Clinical durability alone would not make organs available on demand. That outcome would additionally require sufficient production throughput, pathogen screening, dependable distribution and clinical capacity to perform and support transplantation. Production facilities are being developed, but the supplied reports do not establish routine supply sufficient to meet patient demand. The revolutionary impact therefore depends on achieving clinical performance and operational availability together.

Conditional impact synthesis: success with kidneys could encourage development of animal liver, heart and lung transplantation, but it would not demonstrate those capabilities. Each organ would require its own evidence of physiological function, safety and durability. Likewise, replacing an organ does not by itself regenerate the recipient’s damaged native tissue, eliminate immunosuppression or establish the ability to assemble human organs outside the body.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central unsolved capability in this evidence set is reliable years-long xenograft function across recipients while maintaining acceptable clinical risks. Donor genetic editing and recipient immunosuppression have supported months of kidney function, but the supplied observations do not demonstrate the combined achievement of multi-year destination therapy and production at patient-demand scale. These selected reports also cannot establish that no other relevant results exist elsewhere in the field.

A concrete clinical barrier is balancing rejection control against infection risk. In the reported 271-day kidney case, early T-cell-mediated rejection resolved with treatment. Later, immunosuppression was reduced during a non-zoonotic bacterial infection; microvascular injury subsequently progressed to thrombotic microangiopathy, involving injury and clotting in small blood vessels, and the graft failed. This sequence illustrates the need to preserve immune protection and vascular integrity during intercurrent illness. A single case does not establish the frequency of this failure pathway or prove that the treatment change alone caused it.

Further barriers include detecting and limiting animal-pathogen transmission, determining whether exposure sensitizes recipients in ways that compromise later human transplantation, and producing consistently suitable organs. Negative pathogen surveillance and unchanged anti-HLA antibodies in one recipient are encouraging observations, but they do not quantify rare or delayed risks. Designated pathogen-free production infrastructure addresses part of the supply challenge; its existence does not establish adequate throughput, consistent clinical quality or dependable delivery at demand scale.

current_state.text: Riella and colleagues’ Lancet report, published online on 3 September 2026 and in the 12 September issue, describes one living recipient of a gene-edited EGEN-2784 porcine kidney. The accompanying eGenesis release identifies him as Tim Andrews. Transplantation on 25 January 2025 produced immediate graft function and sustained dialysis independence for 271 days. Day-14 T-cell-mediated rejection resolved with treatment. Following reduction of immunosuppression during a non-zoonotic bacterial infection, microvascular injury progressed to thrombotic microangiopathy, causing graft failure and removal. The supplied review used the PubMed abstract rather than the full article; the abstract contains these clinical findings.

In that case, no porcine pathogen transmission was detected and anti-HLA antibodies remained unchanged. A human kidney transplanted 82 days after xenograft removal functioned immediately, with no evidence of sensitization during 231 days of follow-up. The observation demonstrates prolonged dialysis-free support followed by successful human kidney transplantation. It does not establish multi-year destination therapy, population-level infection safety or the general absence of sensitization after xenotransplantation.

On 3 September 2026, eGenesis reported that five patients had received EGEN-2784 kidneys under expanded access since March 2024. According to the company, three had achieved more than eight months of dialysis-free function, one remained dialysis-free beyond nine months, and two had transitioned to human kidneys. The company also reported FDA clearance for RESTORE, a 33-patient phase 1/2/3 study, with initiation expected in the first quarter of 2027. These are company-reported observations and plans, rather than a peer-reviewed outcome series; clearance and an anticipated start date do not establish trial results.

United Therapeutics announced on 3 November 2025 that the first transplant in EXPAND, NCT06878560, had been performed at NYU Langone Health using its 10-gene-edit UKidney. The combined phase 1/2/3 study planned efficacy assessments over 24 weeks and lifelong monitoring. Its stated outcome domains included graft and participant survival, kidney function, infections and other adverse events. The announcement reported the transplant operation and study design, without recipient efficacy outcomes. It is a company release, including in its retained PDF form.

A separate United Therapeutics release dated 20 October 2026 announced its third designated pathogen-free xenograft production facility. It reported that the first facility opened in Christiansburg, Virginia, in 2024 to supply ongoing clinical trials, while two newer facilities were designed for commercial scaling following approval. This documents production infrastructure and investment, rather than demonstrated commercial throughput or routine supply sufficient to meet patient demand. The release described the company’s xenotransplant products as investigational and unapproved in any jurisdiction for any indication.

Evidence scope: the supplied materials document months of living-recipient kidney support, expanded-access experience, formal trial initiation and production-facility development. They do not demonstrate the full combined capability described here. The latest relevant retained release is dated 20 October 2026, and no search-coverage record was supplied to establish an exhaustive field-wide status as of 1 November 2026. The earlier account of a 2024 kidney functioning for 52 days cannot be assessed from these materials because its cited investigators’ release is absent; that evidence gap does not establish that the account is false.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed clinical demonstration: a prospective study with a prespecified sample size sufficient to estimate failure rates and their uncertainty shows that most recipients of genetically edited porcine kidneys retain functioning grafts and remain off dialysis for several years. Before enrollment, investigators would define the numerical meaning of most, the follow-up duration, adequate kidney function and treatment failure. Graft survival, recipient survival and dialysis independence should be reported separately so that one favorable measure cannot conceal deterioration in another. These are proposed criteria, not established standards in the supplied sources.
completion_criteria.label: Most porcine kidney recipients maintain dialysis-independent graft function for years

completion_criteria.text: Proposed comparative and safety demonstration: prespecified, clinically justified comparisons with human deceased-donor kidney transplantation assess rejection, infection, graft failure and death in comparable recipient populations. Surveillance would report methods, duration and findings for pig-pathogen transmission, alongside ordinary infection risks and immunosuppression burden. Demonstrating no sustained transmission during stated follow-up would be meaningful, while leaving uncertainty about rarer events and longer time horizons. Follow-up of subsequent human transplantation would also help assess sensitization and the practicality of rescue options.
completion_criteria.label: Prespecified comparisons assess safety against human deceased-donor kidney transplantation

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and supply demonstration: results recur across clinical teams, sites and production batches, with transparent reporting of unsuccessful transplants and withdrawals. Production and delivery meet a defined clinical demand over a sustained period, with measured throughput, organ suitability, screening performance and delivery reliability. The demonstrated indication, recipient population, donor design and management regimen would define the initial practical boundaries. Finite studies could establish reproducible benefit across those conditions; they would not establish safety for every patient, indefinite graft survival or success with other organs.
completion_criteria.label: Reproducible transplant benefit and sustained supply meet defined clinical demand

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: CLM-01, Programmable antigen-specific immune tolerance, overlaps with the challenge of preventing graft rejection. Successful tolerance could potentially reduce the immunosuppression burden of xenotransplantation. Durable xenograft function does not itself demonstrate tolerance, and the supplied evidence does not establish that CLM-01 is a necessary or exclusive route to achieving it.

Current clinical xenotransplantation remains distinct from freedom from immunosuppressive treatment. The EXPAND announcement states that transplant recipients require immunosuppressive medication, and the reported EGEN-2784 case illustrates the clinical tension between maintaining that treatment and managing infection.

Roster-based synthesis: CLM-06, Therapeutic remuscularization of the adult human heart, seeks to restore muscle in a recipient’s existing heart. Cardiac xenotransplantation would instead provide a replacement animal heart. CLM-15, Restoration of nephron number in the adult human kidney, similarly concerns restoring the kidney’s filtering units, whereas porcine kidney transplantation supplies function through a donor organ. Shared goals of recovering organ function do not make these the same innovation.

Roster-based synthesis: CLM-11, Implantable human-scale organs assembled outside the body, shares the goal of providing transplantable replacement organs through a scalable source. Its defining capability is external assembly of human-scale organs; CLM-05 centers on organs obtained from animal donors. Advances in implantation, organ assessment or production logistics could be relevant to both, but achievement of either capability would not establish the other.

unresolved_issues: The supplied evidence does not establish exhaustive field-wide status as of 1 November 2026 or subsequent developments.

Full-text methods and results from the 2026 Lancet report were not available in the reviewed material; conclusions remain limited to the retained abstract and separately attributed company information.
The GAO waiting-list and mortality figures and the 2024 52-day kidney account remain unverified in this evidence set.
Population-level rates of graft failure, rejection, ordinary infection, animal-pathogen transmission, sensitization and death remain undetermined by the supplied single-case and company reports.
Whether multi-year xenograft function can be maintained with an acceptable immunosuppression burden, including during intercurrent infection, remains unresolved.
The numerical thresholds for clinical success, follow-up duration, acceptable comparative risks and sufficient production scale require prospective definition.
Facility announcements do not resolve actual throughput, consistency, delivery reliability or the clinical capacity needed to meet patient demand.
The roster provides titles rather than full definitions of related innovations; their detailed technical dependencies cannot be established from these inputs.

brief.title: Long-lasting animal organs for people who need them
possible: People who need a replacement organ could receive one from an animal, with a dependable supply to meet demand. For someone with kidney failure, a genetically edited pig kidney could mean years without dialysis, a treatment for kidney failure.
why: Transplantation could become much less dependent on scarce human donor organs. For kidney patients, sustained freedom from dialysis could come with acceptable treatment burdens and risks.

sources.showed: A genetically edited pig kidney supported a living recipient for months before failing. The patient later received a functioning human kidney.
sources.quote: No porcine pathogen transmission was detected.
sources.cited_for: Pig kidneys can provide prolonged support while preserving the possibility of a later human kidney transplant.
sources.not_established: This single case does not establish years of reliable function or the frequency of rejection, infection and other harms.

sources.showed: The company reported that several recipients had sustained kidney function without dialysis for months, and that some later received human kidneys.
sources.quote: have successfully transitioned to human donor kidney transplants.
sources.cited_for: Company-reported experience extends months of dialysis-free function beyond the published case.
sources.not_established: These company reports do not establish reliable long-term outcomes across recipients.

sources.who: United Therapeutics and NYU Langone Health
sources.showed: United Therapeutics reported the first pig kidney transplant in its EXPAND clinical trial, which will assess kidney function, survival and safety.
sources.quote: The successful transplant operation was performed at NYU Langone Health.
sources.cited_for: A formal clinical trial has begun testing genetically edited pig kidneys.
sources.not_established: A completed transplant operation does not establish lasting kidney function or acceptable risks.

shown: Riella and colleagues reported that a pig kidney kept a recipient off dialysis for 271 days. After immune-suppressing treatment was reduced during a bacterial infection, injury and clotting in small blood vessels led to kidney failure. The patient later received a functioning human kidney.

eGenesis has reported months without dialysis in several recipients, although these results are company reports rather than a peer-reviewed series. United Therapeutics has begun a clinical trial and developed production facilities.
missing: Reliable kidney function lasting years across recipients, with acceptable risks and treatment burdens, remains to be demonstrated.
Larger studies must establish how often animal infections pass to people and whether pig organs complicate later human transplants.
Consistent production, screening and delivery sufficient to meet patient demand remain to be demonstrated.

milestones.label: Most pig kidney recipients stay off dialysis for years
milestones.explanation: A study large enough to estimate failure rates would have to show that most recipients stay off dialysis for years under predefined success criteria. This would establish durable kidney replacement.

milestones.label: Safety is assessed against human donor kidney transplants
milestones.explanation: Predefined comparisons with kidneys from deceased human donors would have to assess rejection, infection, kidney failure and death in comparable patients. This would establish how the risks compare.

milestones.label: Repeatable benefits and dependable supply meet defined demand
milestones.explanation: Benefits would have to recur across teams, hospitals and production batches while reliable organ production and delivery meet defined demand over time. This would establish a dependable service for patients.

uncertain: Can treatment prevent immune attacks on pig kidneys without imposing an unacceptable infection risk, including during other illnesses?
How often will recipients develop immune responses that make a later human transplant harder?
What thresholds should define clinical success, acceptable comparative risks and sufficient supply?

page.title: Licensed pig organ xenotransplantation
page.definition: A whole organ from a pig is implanted in a living patient to take over a failing organ’s function. The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) licenses the specific organ product for a defined clinical use, with evidence for that use and controls on production. Investigational pig kidneys have reached clinical trials. FDA also uses the term xenotransplantation for animal cells, tissues and certain procedures involving contact with animal material outside the body.

goal.need: The number of US organ donors grew by 87% from 2015 to 2024, yet more than 100,000 people were waiting for a transplant in May 2025. A supply of pig organs could give patients a transplant before a human donor becomes available. For someone with kidney failure, that could mean time off dialysis while waiting for a human kidney, or a longer-term replacement if the graft keeps working. Kidney trial recipients need lifelong monitoring for infections that can pass from pigs to people.

completion.title: FDA licenses a pig whole-organ product for clinical transplantation.
completion.criterion: FDA issues a biologics licence for a pig whole-organ product for replacement of failed human-organ function. Approval covers a specified product, indication and manufacturing process; the product and manufacturing establishments must meet the application's standards and applicable regulations. Achievement is assessed separately for each organ. The approved indication and evidence determine the demonstrated duration of benefit.
completion.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, biologics licensing framework and 21 CFR 601.20.
completion.threshold_quote: FDA approval to market a biologic is granted by issuance of a biologics license.
completion.basis: Licensure combines assessment of the organ product with manufacturing controls. It supplies an external test for clinical use, without establishing a universal graft lifespan or demand-matching production volume. United Therapeutics reported on 20 October 2026 that its xenotransplant organs remained unapproved in every jurisdiction.

milestones.title: Preclinical pig-organ studies justify initial human exposure.
milestones.criterion: The sponsor provides enough pharmacology and toxicology data from laboratory animals or in vitro studies to conclude that the proposed human investigation is reasonably safe. The nature and duration of that investigation determine the kind, duration and scope of testing required.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 312.23(a)(8) and its 2016 xenotransplantation guidance, section IX.
milestones.threshold_quote: on the basis of which the sponsor has concluded that it is reasonably safe to conduct the proposed clinical investigations.

milestones.title: An investigational pig organ is transplanted into a living human.
milestones.criterion: A living human recipient undergoes transplantation of the investigational pig organ. A documented implantation under expanded access or in a clinical trial qualifies at the time of surgery.
milestones.set_by: Clinical first-in-human convention, reflected in FDA 21 CFR 312.21(a)(1). Expanded-access treatments establish human use without constituting a completed phase 1 trial.
milestones.threshold_quote: Phase 1 includes the initial introduction of an investigational new drug into humans.

milestones.title: An investigational new drug application takes effect for a prospective US pig-organ trial.
milestones.criterion: The sponsor submits an investigational new drug application (IND) covering the prospective trial. The IND takes effect 30 days after FDA receives it unless FDA places the investigation on clinical hold, or earlier if FDA notifies the sponsor that the investigation may begin. The sponsor and investigators must comply with applicable requirements for trial conduct, informed consent and institutional review.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 312.40.
milestones.threshold_quote: Thirty days after FDA receives the IND, unless FDA notifies the sponsor that the investigations described in the IND are subject to a clinical hold

milestones.title: Studies establish a pig-organ product's safety, purity and potency for its proposed indication.
milestones.criterion: For the proposed indication, data from nonclinical laboratory studies and clinical studies demonstrate that the manufactured pig-organ product meets the prescribed requirements for safety, purity and potency.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 601.2(a).
milestones.threshold_quote: data derived from nonclinical laboratory and clinical studies which demonstrate that the manufactured product meets prescribed requirements of safety, purity, and potency

milestones.title: FDA inspection establishes that a pig-organ product's manufacturing establishments meet licensing standards.
milestones.criterion: FDA inspects the establishments listed in the pig-organ product’s biologics license application and determines that they comply with the standards in that application and the requirements of applicable regulations.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 601.20(d).
milestones.threshold_quote: upon a determination that the establishment(s) complies with the standards established in the biologics license application and the requirements prescribed in applicable regulations.

milestones.title: A transplanted pig organ performs its intended function in a preclinical recipient.
milestones.criterion: A preclinical transplant study measures a function of the implanted pig organ in a recipient of another species and shows that the graft supplies that function. The measure must be appropriate to the organ under study.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, 2016 xenotransplantation guidance, section IX.A, on preclinical assessment of product function.
milestones.threshold_quote: the determination of function of the xenotransplantation product

milestones.title: Review of the first recipients’ outcomes permits a staged pig-organ trial to expand enrollment.
milestones.criterion: In a trial with staged enrollment, safety and efficacy data from the initial recipients undergo the review specified for expansion. In kidney EXPAND, an independent data monitoring committee decides whether to proceed after the initial cohort of six reaches at least 12 weeks post-transplant. In heart EXPRESS, expansion beyond two recipients follows FDA review of data from those two transplants. Each threshold applies only to its named trial.
milestones.set_by: United Therapeutics, EXPAND kidney and EXPRESS heart clinical trial protocols.
milestones.threshold_quote: an Independent Data Monitoring Committee to determine if the study should proceed to the next cohort.

not_found: No universal minimum human graft lifespan or demand-matching production threshold was found in FDA guidance, IXA position papers or the cited trial descriptions.
The EXPAND registry page did not expose its outcome details; no public numerical overall trial-success cutoff was located.
No completed pivotal outcome dataset or whole-organ marketing licence was located for kidney, heart, liver or lung xenotransplantation.
No FDA clearance for an implanted pig-liver or pig-lung prospective clinical trial was located.

results.finding: In one expanded-access recipient, the transplanted pig heart failed on post-transplant day 49.

results.finding: The FDA authorized a genetically engineered pig heart transplant for 1 patient under expanded access after reviewing preclinical primate data.
results.detail: The preclinical evidence supported an individualized decision for a patient with no remaining treatment options. The article does not state the number of animals in the FDA submission.
results.quote: The FDA approved our request on December 31st, 2021, after reviewing our preclinical data of multi-gene pig heart transplantation into NHPs.

results.finding: One Tibetan macaque survived 4 days after orthotopic transplantation of a ten-gene-edited pig liver.

results.finding: In one nephrectomized human decedent, the transplanted pig kidney supported an estimated glomerular filtration rate above 100 mL/min/1.73 m².
results.detail: The study estimated filtration using the 2021 CKD-EPI equation. Estimated filtration declined during antibody-mediated rejection and rose after treatment.

results.finding: An orthotopic pig liver graft in one brain-deceased human produced albumin and bile throughout 11 days of observation.
results.detail: Microthrombosis impaired hepatic perfusion and likely contributed to late functional decline. The study also observed progressive thrombocytopenia and reduced clotting factor activity.
results.quote: Throughout the 11-day observation period, the xenograft maintains continuous albumin and bile production with normal composition, albeit at a relatively low level.

results.finding: A pig lung graft in one brain-dead human recipient (n=1) was reported to remain functional for 216 hours.
results.detail: The 216 hours quantify the monitoring period. The excerpt does not provide a graft-specific gas-exchange measurement.
results.quote: The lung xenograft maintained viability and functionality over the course of the 216 hours of the monitoring period, without signs of hyperacute rejection or infection.

definition = "A whole organ from a pig is implanted in a living patient to take over a failing organ\u2019s function. The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) licenses the specific organ product for a defined clinical use, with evidence for that use and controls on production. Investigational pig kidneys have reached clinical trials. FDA also uses the term xenotransplantation for animal cells, tissues and certain procedures involving contact with animal material outside the body.". Reason: The definition gains a concrete comparison with an investigational transplant and makes the whole-organ scope explicit within FDA's broader use of xenotransplantation.

goal.need = "The number of US organ donors grew by 87% from 2015 to 2024, yet more than 100,000 people were waiting for a transplant in May 2025. A supply of pig organs could give patients a transplant before a human donor becomes available. For someone with kidney failure, that could mean time off dialysis while waiting for a human kidney, or a longer-term replacement if the graft keeps working. Kidney trial recipients need lifelong monitoring for infections that can pass from pigs to people.". Reason: The waiting-list count gains a comparison with growth in human donation, a concrete benefit for patients on dialysis and the condition under which that benefit lasts.

add statement by National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, 2024: "developing safe and effective strategies to enable clinical xenotransplantation.". Reason: The funding notice documents a US government programme that explicitly set clinical translation as the goal of its preclinical work.

add statement by People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals, 2024: "Pigs are not merely housing their organs until humans need them.". Reason: The animal advocacy organisation's statement records an ethical objection to using pigs as organ donors.

add milestone after None: "A transplanted pig organ performs its intended function in a preclinical recipient.". Reason: Demonstrating organ function in a preclinical model is an observable laboratory result that precedes the broader safety judgment required for human exposure.

edit m1: criterion = "The sponsor provides enough pharmacology and toxicology data from laboratory animals or in vitro studies to conclude that the proposed human investigation is reasonably safe. The nature and duration of that investigation determine the kind, duration and scope of testing required."; threshold_quote = "on the basis of which the sponsor has concluded that it is reasonably safe to conduct the proposed clinical investigations."; threshold_ref = 8; refs = [8, 5]. Reason: The revision identifies who makes the preclinical safety judgment and removes the kidney and lung observations from the test.

edit m2: criterion = "A living human recipient undergoes transplantation of the investigational pig organ. A documented implantation under expanded access or in a clinical trial qualifies at the time of surgery."; threshold_quote = "Phase 1 includes the initial introduction of an investigational new drug into humans."; threshold_ref = 11; refs = [11, 12]. Reason: The criterion isolates the first implant in a living recipient from subsequent graft survival and from studies in deceased recipients.

edit m3: title = "An investigational new drug application takes effect for a prospective US pig-organ trial."; criterion = "The sponsor submits an investigational new drug application (IND) covering the prospective trial. The IND takes effect 30 days after FDA receives it unless FDA places the investigation on clinical hold, or earlier if FDA notifies the sponsor that the investigation may begin. The sponsor and investigators must comply with applicable requirements for trial conduct, informed consent and institutional review."; threshold_quote = "Thirty days after FDA receives the IND, unless FDA notifies the sponsor that the investigations described in the IND are subject to a clinical hold"; threshold_ref = 15; refs = [15]. Reason: The title and criterion now cover both ways an IND can take effect and distinguish permission to conduct a trial from a transplant performed in it.

add milestone after m3: "Review of the first recipients’ outcomes permits a staged pig-organ trial to expand enrollment.". Reason: The kidney and heart protocols specify a review of the first recipients before enrollment can expand, a distinct step between trial clearance and evidence for licensure.

edit m4: criterion = "For the proposed indication, data from nonclinical laboratory studies and clinical studies demonstrate that the manufactured pig-organ product meets the prescribed requirements for safety, purity and potency."; set_by = "US Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 601.2(a)."; threshold_quote = "data derived from nonclinical laboratory and clinical studies which demonstrate that the manufactured product meets prescribed requirements of safety, purity, and potency"; threshold_ref = 18; refs = [18]. Reason: The revision keeps the licensing evidence standard and removes trial schedules and interim reporting status from the pass criterion.
